1.  **Alpha particle (I):** An alpha particle is a helium nucleus consisting of 2 protons and 2 neutrons. Its mass is approximately $6.64 \times 10^{-27}$ kg (or about 4 atomic mass units).
2.  **Neutron (G) & Proton (J):** These are nucleons. A neutron has a mass of approximately $1.675 \times 10^{-27}$ kg, and a proton is slightly lighter. Both are roughly 1 atomic mass unit.
3.  **Other options:** Electrons, positrons, beta particles, muons, and neutrinos are significantly lighter than nucleons. Photons are massless. Quarks are fundamental constituents of protons and neutrons; while the top quark is very heavy, the generic term "quark" usually refers to the class or lighter varieties (up/down) in general contexts, and alpha particles are explicitly defined composite particles with a definite mass greater than individual nucleons.

Since an alpha particle is composed of four nucleons, it is significantly more massive than a single neutron, proton, or any of the lighter leptons listed.
